items.text: Keep the infant heir's body and goods faithfully and give a full account when he comes of age.
items.citation: Perambulation of Kent, Customes of Kent
items.quote: committe the nouriture of the body, and the custodie of the goods, and landes of the infant, to the next of the kinred... the Lord may distreine the Gardien to yeelde his accompt

items.text: Keep himself a widower and unmarried if he would retain his late wife's land; marrying again forfeits it.
items.citation: Perambulation of Kent, Customes of Kent
items.quote: shall hold the same during so long time, as he wil kéepe him selfe widower, and vnmarried. For if he marrie, he looseth all.
items.conflict: Conflicts with 1 Cor 7:39, which permits remarriage after a spouse's death.

heading: The Customes of Kent.

items.text: Defend and discharge the warranty your father gave; do not leave it to the eldest alone, for all the heirs in gavelkind are to be vouched.
items.citation: A Perambulation of Kent, The Customes of Kent
items.quote: all the Heires in Gauelkind shalbe vouched for the warrantie of their auncestour, and not the eldest only

items.text: Pay your father's debts out of the inheritance; all of you who have assets are charged.
items.citation: A Perambulation of Kent, The Customes of Kent
items.quote: they all shalbe charged for the debte of their auncestour, if so be that they all have Assetz in their handes

heading: The Customes of Kent.

items.text: As guardian, take charge of the child's upbringing and his lands, keep him until he is fifteen, and account to the heir for all receipts.
items.citation: Perambulation of Kent, The Customes of Kent
items.quote: the next Cousin, to whome the inheritance may not descend, shal haue the education, & order of his body, & landes

heading: The Customes of Kent.

items.text: Allow your younger brothers their equal share of the gavelkind land when they claim it, for the land remains partible among all male heirs.
items.citation: Perambulation of Kent, The Customes of Kent
items.quote: the lande remayneth partible betwéene them, when so euer they will put to theyr claime.

items.text: Let your brother's daughter join with you in the partition, for she stands in her father's place as his heir.
items.citation: Perambulation of Kent, The Customes of Kent
items.quote: the daughter shall ioyne with the two other Brethren her Vncles

work: A Perambulation of Kent: 'The Customes of Kent' and the Custumal of Kent with hi
heading: The Customes of Kent.

items.text: Allow your widowed mother the moiety of your father's lands for her life, as the custom of Kent provides.
items.quote: The wyfe lykewyse, after the death of her Husband, shall haue for her lyfe, the one moitie of all such landes of Gauelkind tenure, whereof her Husband was seised of any estate of inheritance during the couerture betwéene them.

items.text: Do not remarry, on pain of losing your dower, as the custom forbids remarriage.
items.quote: One, that she may not marrie at all.
items.conflict: 1 Cor 7:39: 'A wife is bound as long as her husband lives; but if her husband is dead, she is free to be married to whom she will, only in the Lord.'

items.text: Keep yourself from fornication, especially from bearing a child; if such a child is born and heard to cry, you forfeit your dower.
items.quote: she must take diligent héede, that she be not found with Childe, begottē in fornicatiō. For in either case she must loose her Dower.

items.text: Do not withhold her dower on account of her husband's felony unless the inheritance itself is forfeited.
items.quote: if the husband commit Felonie: at the common law, his wife hath lost her title of Dower, but by the custome of this countrey, she shall not loose her Dower for the faulte of her husbande, but only in suche case, where the heire shall loose his inheritance, for the offence of his father.

items.text: Give her a share of your father's goods: half if he died childless, a third if he left children.
items.quote: prouideth Dower of the moitie of suche goods also, as he dyed possessed of, if he had no children, and of the thirde part, though he leaue issue.

heading: The Custumal of Kent, with Lambarde's interlinear English

items.text: When your father dies, endow his widow with half the gavelkind lands he held, to be hers as long as she remains a widow.
items.citation: Custumal of Kent, with Lambarde's interlinear English
items.quote: let that wife by and by be endowed (of the one halfe of the tenements wherof her husbande dyed vested & seised) by the heires

items.text: Allow your late mother's widower to hold half her gavelkind lands as long as he remains a widower and commits no waste.
items.citation: Custumal of Kent, with Lambarde's interlinear English
items.quote: let the husband haue the one halfe of those landes and tenementes whereof she died seised so long as he holdeth him a widower

items.text: When inheriting gavelkind land, let all sons (or daughters if no sons) divide it into equal shares.
items.citation: Custumal of Kent, with Lambarde's interlinear English
items.quote: all his sonnes shall parte that inheritaunce by equall portions. And if there be no heire male, let the partition be made betweene the females

items.text: If the hearth-place (Astre) falls to you as the youngest, pay your co-heirs their share of its value.
items.citation: Custumal of Kent, with Lambarde's interlinear English
items.quote: the youngest make reasonable amendes to his parceners for the part which to them belongeth

items.text: Let the eldest brother choose his portion first; then the next in order.
items.citation: Custumal of Kent, with Lambarde's interlinear English
items.quote: let the eldest brother haue the first choyce, & the others afterward, according to their degree

items.text: Contribute your share to the co-heir who performs the single court suit on behalf of all the parceners.
items.citation: Custumal of Kent, with Lambarde's interlinear English
items.quote: let al ye parceners make contribution to ye parcener which maketh ye suite for them

items.text: When the heir reaches fifteen, deliver to him all his lands, goods, and the profits above his reasonable sustenance, and give an account of your stewardship.
items.citation: Custumal of Kent, with Lambarde's interlinear English
items.quote: when suche heire... shall come to the full age of fifteene yeares, let their lands and tenements be deliuered vnto them, together with their goods, and with the emprouements profits... of the which profits and goods, let him be bounde to make aunswere which had ye education of the heire
